ground_truth.description: The freshly created module from `module_from_spec` is executed via `exec_module` without first being registered in `sys.modules` under its synthetic name. The Python docs recommend inserting the module into `sys.modules` before `exec_module` so that self-referential or circular imports within the module resolve correctly; omitting it can make the isolated load fail (or behave differently from a real import) if the production module ever imports itself.

`test_escalation_attribute_is_bound` hard-asserts `mod._HAS_ESCALATION is True`, coupling the test to the assumption that the escalation package is always installed. Unlike the previous test (which forced the unavailable branch), this new assertion will fail in any environment where escalation is not installed, reducing portability of the test suite.

task.title: Clean up post-task-1204 _HAS_ESCALATION artifacts: drop production flag and simplify TestEscalationBinding
task.description: Task 1204 made `Escalation` unconditionally bound (None on ImportError), rendering both `_HAS_ESCALATION` in production code and the importlib.reload-based TestEscalationBinding test redundant. Remove the production flag and replace the reload test with a lighter verification mechanism in one pass.
task.details:
FILES_TO_MODIFY:
  - fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/stage1_stall_detector.py
  - fused-memory/tests/reconciliation/test_stage1_stall_detector.py

DETAILS:
Context: review suggestions on task 1204 (reviewer_comprehensive). Both items are non-blocking cleanup that must be done together — removing `_HAS_ESCALATION` from production voids the `mod._HAS_ESCALATION is False` assertion at test line 469, which is the very assertion the reload test exists to verify.

**Part A — Drop `_HAS_ESCALATION` from production code**
`fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/stage1_stall_detector.py` lines 64-69:
- Remove `_HAS_ESCALATION = True` from the try branch.
- Remove `_HAS_ESCALATION = False` from the except ImportError branch.
- The import block then reads: try `from escalation.models import Escalation`; except ImportError: `Escalation = None  # type: ignore[assignment,misc]`.
- Verify no other modules reference `_HAS_ESCALATION` (confirmed none do at time of spawn).

**Part B — Replace importlib.reload-based TestEscalationBinding with lighter verification**
`fused-memory/tests/reconciliation/test_stage1_stall_detector.py` lines 425-479:
- The current class reloads the entire module with a poisoned sys.modules entry and asserts `mod._HAS_ESCALATION is False` (line 469). The reload blast radius is large — every module-level attribute is rebound.
- Preferred replacement (option (a) from reviewer):
  - Add a top-level `assert hasattr(stage1_stall_detector, 'Escalation')` check (catches regressions that drop the binding when the package IS installed in CI).
  - Add a static/AST check that the `except ImportError` branch in `stage1_stall_detector.py` contains the literal `Escalation = None` assignment (catches the regression even when CI has escalation installed).
  - Drop the `sys.modules` injection and the documented reload footgun warning from the class docstring.
- Alternative (option (b)): keep the reload but enforce ordering so this class runs last in the file; document that no module-level patches may rely on stage1_stall_detector being import-stable across this test.
- Either way, remove the `mod._HAS_ESCALATION is False` assertion at line 469 — `_HAS_ESCALATION` no longer exists after Part A.

Reviewer: reviewer_comprehensive
Source: post-merge review of task 1204
Severity: non-blocking cleanup
